name: Branded Queue / Waiting Room

transitions.precondition: `getWaitingRoomPosition` answers `admitted`. The page keeps `admission.token` and sends it as `X-Admission-Token` on `addCartLine` until `admission.expiresAt`
transitions.provenance: ADR-0066 (accepted 1 October 2026) and its 1 October amendment

notes: **The on-sale waiting room (Q2), not the ride queue (Q1). Re-pointed 1 October under ADR-0066** from `joinQueue`, `getWaitingGuest` and `getWaitTimes`, which are the ride queue and wrote a `queue.entry` row per arriving guest, the load the room exists to keep away. The ride queue stays on WEB-040. Arrival is `enterWaitingRoom` (a Redis counter, no database write, no sign-in, no personal data); the page polls `getWaitingRoomPosition` every `pollAfterSeconds`. Admitted, it holds a short-lived signed admission token that `addCartLine` needs for this performance while its room is on (online cart holds only: the 1 October amendment exempts tills, kiosks and venue workstations). **Reached from the sale, not the home screen:** WEB-006 lands here when `addCartLine` refuses `403 admission-required`, and admission returns there. `notRequired` (the room is off) goes straight back. **Renamed 31 August** from *Virtual Waiting Room*. **A guest surface is one product with two renderings** (GST-046).
patternReason: `getWaitingRoomPosition` reads one guest's place in one performance's room, polled — the screen is about that one thing
purpose: The on-sale waiting room for one performance — the guest's place, the wait, and the way on to the sale once admitted.

components.label: Your place in the waiting room
Take my place
components.notes: The one write on this screen, pressed rather than fired on load so a prefetch or a bot does not take a place. Hidden once the guest has one.

states.loading: Taking a place in the room. *Take my place* (`enterWaitingRoom`) answers with a position, or `notRequired` and the guest goes straight on to the sale
states.error: **Lost the place.** The worst failure on this screen. A retry sends the same `Idempotency-Key` and gets the same entry back, so the guest is not sent to the back, and the screen says so, because a guest who thinks they lost their place will open a second tab and make it worse. `expired` (the admission was not used in time) offers to enter again; `closed` (the room was switched off or the performance stopped selling) says so and goes back to the event
states.emptyNoAccess: **There is no access to refuse.** The room is anonymous (ADR-0066): no sign-in, no personal data, and the guest may not have an account yet.
states.offline: **The offline banner shows.** The last known position stays on screen with its age, and polling resumes with the same entry when the connection is back. Admission needs the connection.

apis.purpose: Take a place in the performance's on-sale waiting room (ADR-0066); `notRequired` when the room is off
The guest's place, polled every `pollAfterSeconds`; admitted, it carries the admission token for `addCartLine`

entryState.coldEntry: **Opened with no performance, or one no longer selling, the room says so and offers the event** — never a 404. The room belongs to one performance's sale and has nothing to show without one.

prototype.view: Only when the host tweak 'waitingRoom' is on; it is not in the Config drawer lists, so a reviewer cannot switch it on from the page
prototype.differences: Drawn but unreachable from the Config drawer. The prototype holds the place by keeping the page open ('refreshing puts you at the back'); the room keeps it across a refresh, because `enterWaitingRoom` returns the same entry for the same `Idempotency-Key` (ADR-0066). **The copy must not say "refreshing puts you at the back"**: the room keeps the place across a refresh (same entry for the same Idempotency-Key, ADR-0066) (CHG-SGU-020).

apisNote: Rebuilt 1 October 2026 on the two waiting-room operations (ADR-0066). Columns are the entry's guest-facing fields; `pollAfterSeconds` and `admission` are plumbing the page acts on rather than shows.

offlineBanner.message: You're offline. Connect to the internet to book, pay, order or join a queue.
offlineBanner.shows: The moment the connection drops, on every screen, above the screen's own content.
offlineBanner.clears: By itself as soon as the connection is back, with a short "Back online" confirmation.
offlineBanner.never: Covers what is already on screen, or appears for a server error — that is the screen's own error state, and a guest told they are offline when the venue is down reconnects for nothing.
offlineBanner.provenance: Decided 12 September 2026 — guest web and guest app behave identically offline and say so with the same banner.

targetApp.name: TICVAI Guest
targetApp.note: **One guest product in three shells.** Web, mobile and kiosk share 73–91% of their operations; the kiosk is the same product in a fixed frame with no keyboard, and is deliberately narrower rather than different.
